title: Enterprise bulk data ingest, backfill, and live cutover playbook
author: Alyssa Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook provides a prescriptive, low-risk process for performing large-scale data ingest and backfill work for enterprise customers, followed by the live cutover to Redwood inference pipelines (hosted, dedicated, or private). It codifies roles, pre-cutover validation, dry-run and backfill strategies, SRE guardrails, escalation paths, rollback criteria, and post-cutover checks.

Scope:
- Target audience: Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Customer SRE, Redwood Platform Ops, and customer engineering teams.
- Applies to: bulk ingestion of telemetry, prompt sets, embedding indices, or any dataset used by inference features where size or throughput requires coordinated cutover.
- Out of scope: routine small-scale batch imports (<100k records) — use standard integration guide.

Goals and success criteria:
- Cutover completes with <1% data loss and no more than 5 minutes of degraded inference latency compared to baseline.
- Backfill throughput sustained to complete within agreed SLA (example: 48 hours for 100M rows).
- No customer-visible errors beyond planned degradation windows; all incidents resolved or rolled back per runbook.

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success (CS): overall cutover coordination, stakeholder comms, runbook lead.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration plan, test harnesses, schema mappings.
- Customer SRE: responsible for customer's production environment, networking, and ACLs.
- Redwood Platform Ops: capacity reservation, dedicated pool config, rollback hooks.
- Redwood SRE/Oncall: live monitoring, alerts, and incident triage.

Contact matrix (primary -> fallback):
- CS lead: alyssa.chen@redwood.ai -> jordan.patel@redwood.ai
- SE lead: ravi.narayanan@redwood.ai -> sofia.martinez@redwood.ai
- Platform Ops pager: #platform-ops -> escalation to oncall@redwood.ai

Pre-cutover checklist (required before any dry run):
1) Contract & SOW confirmation: confirm ingestion SLA, cost model, and storage retention with customer procurement.
2) Capacity and quota reservation: Platform Ops must reserve GPU/CPU pools and token quota for estimated peak load + 30% buffer.
3) Network & permissions validated: firewall rules, VPC peering, service accounts, and KMS/HSM access verified.
4) Schema & mapping validation: SE confirms schema compatibility with runtime and embedding pipelines.
5) Observability hooks enabled: request/response tracing, token-level cost tagging, custom metrics for ingest rate and validation failures.
6) Rollback criteria agreed and documented with sign-off by CS and Customer SRE.

Configuration matrix (example):
| Item | Recommended value | Owner |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| Dedicated pool size | 8x A100 equivalent | Platform Ops |
| Backfill batch size | 5k - 50k records (tune) | SE/Customer |
| Max concurrent streams | 200 | Platform Ops |
| Retention during backfill | 30 days (temp) | Customer |

Pre-run validation tests (execute in staging or shadow environment):
- Synthetic ingest at 1.5x expected rate for 30 minutes to validate autoscaling and queueing.
- Schema edge-case validation (nulls, UTF-8, truncation).
- End-to-end inference correctness checks on representative subset.

Dry-run procedure (recommended and must be green before full backfill):
1) Schedule a 2–4 hour maintenance window with stakeholders and publish comms.
2) Run a limited backfill on a 1–5% subset of data that mirrors distribution.
3) Metrics to observe: ingest success rate >= 99.5%, average token latency within SLO ±10%, error budget < 1%.
4) Run data reconciliation: sample hash checks between source and target for 1000 randomly selected rows.
5) Post-dry-run sign-off meeting: SE, CS, Customer SRE, Platform Ops. If any gate fails, remediate and rerun.

Backfill execution strategy options (choose one):
A) Continuous streaming backfill: best for near-live pipelines, low-latency requirements.
B) Batch windowing with checkpointing: recommended for very large datasets (>=50M rows) to limit peak load.
C) Hybrid (fast-forward then streaming): seed the index with a bulk snapshot, then stream real-time deltas.

Example backfill batch configuration (YAML):
---
batch_size: 20000
parallel_workers: 12
checkpoint_interval: 100000
retry_policy:
  max_retries: 5
  backoff_seconds: 60
validation_checks:
  - checksum
  - schema_match
  - sample_inference_compare
---

Operational monitoring and SLOs during backfill:
- Ingest success rate: target 99.9% (alert if <99.5% for 10m).
- Average per-request latency (inference path): SLO depends on customer tier; e.g., Dedicated <= 150ms p50, <= 500ms p95. Alert if p95 increases >2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Token cost inflation: track cost-per-thousand-tokens; alert if >30% above forecasted.
- Queue depth and backpressure: alert if queue length > 5x normal for 10 minutes.

Incident detection and immediate mitigation steps (triage flow):
1) Detect: Alert fires (one of the SLO alerts above).
2) Triage: Platform Ops and Redwood SRE examine logs, traces, and queue metrics within 10 minutes.
3) Contain: Throttle backfill by reducing parallel_workers or switching to smaller batch_size.
4) Mitigate: Route high-priority customer traffic to fallback model variant or alternative region (see routing policy).
5) Escalate: If containment fails within 20 minutes, page engineering lead and open an incident in PagerDuty.

Escalation matrix (severity mapping):
- Sev3 (performance degradation): CS lead notified, Platform Ops mitigates, 1-hour P1 work window if unresolved.
- Sev2 (partial loss / repeated failures): Page Redwood SRE and SE, require immediate rollback gating.
- Sev1 (customer outage / data loss): Full incident protocol, immediate rollback, legal and exec comms.

Rollback criteria and procedure (pre-agreed):
- Rollback triggers:
  - Data loss detected in reconciliation > 0.5% of sampled rows.
  - Sustained latency >3x SLO for 15+ minutes with no mitigation.
  - Unrecoverable consumer queue corruption.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Stop all ingestion jobs and place system in read-only mode.
  2) Revert model routing to previous stable variant.
  3) Restore snapshot from pre-backfill checkpoint (store snapshots in S3 or customer-provided bucket).
  4) Run reconciliation checks and issue post-mortem.

Post-cutover validation checklist (24–72 hours):
- Full reconciliation completed for initial import window and sampled full dataset.
- Latency and error metrics stable within thresholds.
- Cost report generated and reviewed with CS and customer.
- Retention policy and cold-storage lifecycle rules applied.
- Runbook: close action items and create any follow-ups for engineering or infra.

Telemetry and observability (required tags and dashboards):
- Required metric tags: customer_id, ingest_job_id, batch_id, dataset_name, environment.
- Dashboards to create prior to run: Backfill Overview, Per-job Errors, Cost vs Forecast, Model Latency Heatmap.

Sample CLI commands and checks:
- Kick off a dry-run (example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ingest/run \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -d '{"dataset":"customer_xyz_sample","mode":"dry_run","workers":4}'

- Check backfill job status (example response):
  {
    "job_id": "bf-20260301-01",
    "status": "running",
    "processed": 1200000,
    "failed": 12,
    "eta_minutes": 360
  }

- Reconciliation hash check (pseudo-command):
  redwood-reconcile --source s3://cust-bucket/2026-02-01/ --target redwood://ingest/datasets/customer_xyz --sample 1000 --output reconciliation-report.csv

Cost & billing notes:
- Enable per-job cost tagging before backfill so cost is attributed to customer SOW line items.
- Notify Finance if estimated credit consumption during backfill exceeds committed usage by >20%.

Run completion & sign-off:
- Required sign-offs: SE (schema/mapping), Customer SRE (network/permissions), CS (stakeholder comms), Platform Ops (capacity and final state).
- Closing artifacts to attach to this page: job logs, reconciliation report, cost worksheet, post-mortem if any.

Post-mortem template (if incident during cutover):
1) Summary of incident and impact.
2) Timeline of events (timestamped).
3) Root cause analysis.
4) Corrective actions with owners and due dates.
5) Lessons learned and changes to the runbook.

References and links:
- Integration guide: Event-driven batch ingest connector (internal)
- Network checklist: private-network-firewall-peering-checklist (internal)
- Cost attribution guide: enterprise-telemetry-cost-attribution-connector-playbook

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands and quick checks:
- Verify token usage: redwood-metrics query "sum(tokens) by job_id" --env prod --since 1h
- Inspect queue depth: kubectl -n ingest get hpa,deployments --selector=app=ingest -o wide
- Snapshot restore (example): aws s3 cp s3://backups/customer_xyz/2026-02-09/snapshot.tar.gz /tmp && redwood-restore --file /tmp/snapshot.tar.gz --target dataset/customer_xyz

Document history:
- 2026-02-10: created by Alyssa Chen
- 2026-03-05: edits — added rollback criteria and expansion of monitoring SLOs

If you are the runbook lead and need assistance: page #cs-backfill in Slack or email alyssa.chen@redwood.ai for an immediate consult.
